correctness.rationale: The proof uses the cited published recurrence d(2m)=2d(m) and three odd-index recurrences for m>=3, the published two-sided inequalities and DFA q(2^a)=2. Independently counted distinct Dyck factors of a 32768-symbol Thue–Morse prefix for 1<=n<29, recovering exactly the base equality lists upper [1,2,3,6,12,24], global lower [4,8,16], odd lower [3,5]. Published bounds make the upper inequality strict at every sufficiently large odd n; doubling propagates upper equality exactly. The global lower has only even equality and doubling reduces to powers of two. Odd lower: 4m+3 requires simultaneously m power of two and q(m)=1, contradicting q(2^a)=2; 8m+1 has a stronger lower bound; 8m+5 equality would make consecutive m,m+1 powers of two. This is a complete infinite induction, not an extrapolation from the finite prefix.
residual_risks: Only equality for three specified published bounds, not near-extremizers.
The induction assumes full published recurrence and DFA q properties; an algorithmic prefix enumeration alone does not prove them.
